edit.description: A registration member's NAME parts company with its registration KEY. `RegistrationMember` (:73) carries `key`/`fields`/`members` today and `to_unit` (:116) sets `Unit.id` from `self.key`; what lands is a new `RegistrationMember::name` that joins the collection key with the group's lifted values — generic over the entry shape's lifted fields, so `matcher` is named nowhere in this module — and `to_unit` reading it. For a group-array collection the id becomes the event, then `:` and the matcher's authored bytes (`PostToolUse:Edit|Write`); the key stays the bare event, since `hooks.<Event>` is where the group still writes. The matcher is verbatim, never normalized: `Edit|Write` and `Edit, Write` are two groups and two members. The `event` field the key-field branch (:118-:123) surfaces stays the bare event, so the `hook.enum.event` clause still ranges over a documented value. 0063's one refusal lands at the READ, not at `to_unit`: a matcher carrying `/` is refused loud by `Manifest::parse` (:394) through a new `JsonManifestError` variant, because `to_unit` must stay infallible — `tests/it/common/mod.rs:259` calls it and is out of this entry's fence.

The grammar is UNCHANGED and this entry proves it rather than moving it: `parse_host_address` (:45) already splits at the first colon and the unit test at :252 already pins `rule:a:b` → `("rule", "a:b")`. What lands is the module's own account of the name that now carries one — the doc at :38-:46 names `hook:<Event>:<matcher>` as the real carrier — and a new `/`-refusal predicate the manifest reader judges a matcher by, beside `is_one_segment` (:75) rather than as a `contains('/')` at the caller. It is not `is_one_segment` itself: the qualifier predicate admits the empty spelling, which `is_one_segment` refuses.

Where the joined name lands on a composed member: `manifest_units` (:780) builds every registration member's `Unit` through the changed `to_unit`, so the check side's address for a matcher-bearing hook is the joined one, and a composed handler's host segment reads `hook:<Event>:<matcher>/handler/<n>` by construction — the host segment must be the member name, or a handler under a matcher-bearing group would name no member at all. No behavior of its own moves; what rides is this module's account of the host address. Two members resolving to one address is HOOK-COLLECTION-ADDRESS-DUPLICATE-REFUSAL's, this entry's blocked successor, not this entry's.

Docs only, and the reason is the whole point: the lift's id and the member's NAME part company here. `lifted_registration` (:2132) sets `LiftedMember.id` off `entry.key`, and `LiftedMember`'s doc (:2066) declares that id both the module's `name` property and its file stem — 0074 makes those two facts. The SDK's `hook()` composes the name from event + matcher, so the authored `name` property stays the event and the stem with it: KEEP THE STEM ON THE KEY. `module_stems` (:2194) already allocates `<key>-2` for a second group on one event, and the `GATE_HOOKS` reservation (:226) keys on `hook.event`, so temper's own modules hold the fixed `hooks/<Event>.ts` paths 0073's remedy cites. A stem off the joined name would write `.temper/hooks/PostToolUse:Bash.ts`: `:` and `|` are reserved characters in a Windows file name (learn.microsoft.com/en-us/windows/win32/fileio/naming-a-file, retrieved 2026-09-29), `module_stems`' legality check is the platform's own parent-readback and passes both on unix, temper ships a win32-x64 engine (`.github/workflows/release.yml`), and the scaffold is committed — so one adopter's emit would not check out on another's machine. What moves: `GateHook.event`'s doc (:207) calls the event "the member's identity", now the key alone; `hook_claimed_events` (:1059) claims by EVENT and keeps doing so — a claim is per collection key — reading `registration.key`, never the member name. Out of scope, named not fixed: a manifest key legal on unix and reserved on Windows (an `.mcp.json` server named `a|b`) reaches the same hole with no driver behind it.
The second `member_address` home, kept in step: the same doc-level account of a `:`-carrying name, and the same `/` refusal where the SDK composes one. Decision 0074 names both homes explicitly.

`registrationRows` (:944) spells `key: member.name` — the conflation 0074 breaks. The row's `key` becomes the collection key (the event) while the member's own address keeps the joined name, so `satisfies`/`mention` rows naming a hook re-emit with the matcher and the manifest still writes under `hooks.<Event>`. `tapHookRows` (:999) already dedupes on the (event, matcher) pair, so its rows gain distinct names with no second pass. One incidental to leave alone: two rows on one event now tie on this function's `(kind, key)` sort and the tie resolves by `Array.prototype.sort`'s stability, which keeps groups in authored order — the order Claude Code loads the event's array in. Sorting on the now-distinct names would reorder groups within an event and move `settings.json` bytes for no gain.

`hook` (:523) composes the member's name from its event and matcher rather than taking the event as the whole name, with the join and the collection-key read as named helpers beside `HOOK_MATCHER_KEY` (:510) rather than inline string work; `tapHookRegistration` (:547) follows. This is what makes the two `PostToolUse` taps (`Skill`, `.*`) two members instead of one address twice — the self-host collision decision 0063's Context names.

`registrationFacts` (:774) folds `registrationRows` and `tapHookRows` into the public `RegistrationFact` view and spells the row's key straight through. The split has to survive that map: the facts keep reporting the collection key (`hooks.<Event>`) while the members behind them carry joined names. Verified unchanged at the 5a7c7b97 attempt — the map moves only if the row shape does, and it does not.

Regenerated fixture, not hand-edited, and exactly ONE row churns (measured at the 5a7c7b97 attempt): the `satisfies` member `hook:PreToolUse` (:449) becomes `hook:PreToolUse:Write|Edit|MultiEdit`, since `hooks.ts`'s `hook_guard` binds that matcher. `hook:SessionStart` (:453) is matcher-less and keeps the bare event, and both `registration` rows (:614, :620) keep their event keys.

Identity arms: two groups on one event with distinct matchers are two members at distinct addresses; a matcher-less group keeps the bare event; the address round-trips through `parse_host_address` with the matcher intact; a matcher carrying `/` refuses loud naming the member. Its two existing arms spelling a composed handler's address (:254, :534) drive matcher-less `PreToolUse` fixtures and hold as written — confirm, don't rewrite.

The one arm outside `hook_kind.rs` that spells a composed handler's host address, and the miss that failed the 5a7c7b97 attempt. `explain_narrates_a_composed_handler_member_the_gate_judged` (:1586) drives `ONE_HANDLER_SETTINGS` (:1577), whose one `PreToolUse` group binds `"matcher": "Bash"`, so both literals take the joined form: `explain_in(&harness, "member:hook:PreToolUse/handler/0")` (:1612) becomes `member:hook:PreToolUse:Bash/handler/0`, and the containment assertion `` `PreToolUse` (hook) contains it `` (:1638) becomes `` `PreToolUse:Bash` (hook) contains it ``.

`a_synthesized_tap_hook_projects_its_matcher_group_through_the_registration_loop` (:751) hand-builds the tap `RegistrationRow` with `key: "PostToolUse"` and a `matcher` field — the arm pinning the row shape the SDK derives. It holds under the split: a hook's joined name is derivable from the row's key plus its `matcher` field, so the wire row gains NO field and neither `sdk/src/generated/RegistrationRow.ts` nor `tests/it/seam_bindings_current.rs` moves. If that derivation does not hold, the entry is mis-derived — leave it and raise an open question rather than widening the seam under an entry that never declared it.
The SDK twin's cases for a `:`-bearing name, mirroring the engine's.

The two `PostToolUse` taps with distinct matchers (`.*` and `Skill`, :2166-:2169) are the case that stops colliding: assert two distinctly-named members whose registration rows both key `PostToolUse`, and assert the `/`-matcher refusal at the `hook()` call.

summary: A hook member's name is its event, then `:` and the matcher's authored bytes; the registration key stays the bare event.

tests.asserts: two groups on one event with distinct matchers are two members at distinct addresses, a matcher-less group keeps the bare event, and a matcher carrying `/` refuses loud
`explain` over the one-handler settings fixture resolves the composed handler at `hook:PreToolUse:Bash/handler/0` and narrates its host as `PreToolUse:Bash`
the self-host check stays clean — this repo's six groups become six distinctly-named members and its committed lock names no hook member, so no `.temper/` re-emit is owed

acceptance: cargo test green (the regenerated base-harness fixture accepted; the gauntlet's snapshots must NOT churn — its corpus names no hook member), `pnpm --dir sdk test` green, cargo clippy --all-targets -D warnings clean, cargo fmt --all --check clean.
notes: Decision 0074. DATUM: this repo's `.temper/lock.toml` names NO hook member (6 event-keyed registration rows, all matchers `/`-free), so no human `chore(harness):` re-emit is owed — only the in-fence base-harness fixture re-emits.
